newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Top lots at Christie's jewel sale go unsold.
newsitem.headline: Top lots at Christie's jewel sale go unsold.

text.p: The two top items in a glittering Geneva jewel sale -- a diamond necklace and a brooch that belonged to Queen Margherita of Italy -- failed to meet their reserve prices and went unsold, the auctioneers said on Friday.
However, more than 600 other items sold on Thursday night in the one-day sale in Geneva fetched a total of 38.1 million Swiss francs ($30.5 million), Christie's auction house said.
The unsold royal diamond brooch, whose owner was not disclosed, had a 47.76 carat Colombian emerald in the centre and had been estimated at between $2 million and $2.4 million.

The stunning diamond cascade necklace, a combination of circular, oval, pear and heart-shaped diamonds, had been estimated at 2.7 million Swiss francs ($2.2 million), according to a Christie's spokeswoman. The owner was also not identified.
An unmounted rectangular-cut fancy intense yellow diamond weighing 33.64 carats was bought for more than 1.2 million Swiss francs ($970,800) by Geneva-based Lebanese jeweller Robert Mouawad.

A pair of antique pearl drop and diamond ear-pendants, which also once belonged to Queen Margherita of Savoy-Genoa (1851-1926), were sold to a Hong Kong client for 432,500 Swiss francs ($360,000) -- doubling their estimate. Margherita was the wife of Umberto I, the second King of Italy.

"While we were naturally disappointed not to sell the two top lots of the sale, there was active bidding on the royal emerald brooch and diamond cascade necklace, in each case at 10 per cent below the reserve (price)," Francois Curiel, international jewellery director for Christie's, said.

"Interest was apparent throughout the sale and the reason why the unsold lots failed to sell was because of the reserve and not the desirability of the pieces or state of the market," he added in the statement.

On Wednesday, an emerald and diamond necklace believed to have been the gift of Russian Empress Catherine the Great to a handsome Scot also went unsold when it failed to reach its reserve price at a different sale put on by Sotheby's.

But a pink cushion-shaped diamond thought to have belonged to France's Queen Marie Antoinette and given to her hairdresser before she was forced from the throne, fetched an unexpected 1,7 million Swiss francs ($1,4 million) at the same sale.
